Value Resolve Behavior

withCoreValueBehavior is the core resolve behavior that normalizes plain state values and structured state envelopes into a canonical upstream value for downstream pipeline processing.

This behavior operates exclusively in the Resolve stage. It affects how incoming state inputs are normalized, never when they enter the pipeline or how they are later transformed. No policy evaluation, derivation, or mutation logic occurs as part of value resolution.

State updates may be submitted through the FeatureCell APIs replaceState and mergeState. These APIs accept structured state envelopes that converge on the Resolve stage, where withCoreValueBehavior extracts and normalizes the incoming value.

withCoreValueBehavior operates exclusively in the Resolve stage, executing after interceptors and before operators. It is the pipeline-critical default resolution path for all non-observable, non-deferred, and non-resource inputs.

This behavior resolves structured state envelopes by extracting the value field and forwarding it as a normalized upstream value. An explicit value: null clears state, while an absent or undefined value suppresses downstream processing.

Diagrams
Configuration

withCoreValueBehavior requires no explicit configuration parameters. It is always installed as part of the Resolve stage and participates automatically when a state update is supplied as a plain value or structured state envelope.

This behavior activates when replaceState or mergeState is invoked with a non-observable, non-deferred, and non-resource input. The incoming envelope is normalized during resolution by extracting the value field and producing a canonical upstream value for downstream pipeline stages.

withCoreValueBehavior is pipeline-critical and cannot be disabled or replaced. It serves as the default resolution path for all synchronous state inputs and guarantees deterministic handling of value extraction, state clearing, and suppressed writes.

Examples

withCoreValueBehavior participates automatically when a plain value or structured state envelope is supplied as a state input. No explicit configuration is required during FeatureCell initialization.

In the examples below, a FeatureCell is initialized normally. After initialization, a synchronous state update is submitted using mergeState with a structured state envelope. The Resolve stage extracts the value field and forwards a normalized upstream value to downstream pipeline stages.

Example 1: Resolve a Plain Value State Update

{{`@FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`('employees')
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeService {
  private readonly vault = injectVault`}}<Employee[]>{{`(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    this.vault.initialize();

    const employees = [
      { id: 1, name: 'Alice' },
      { id: 2, name: 'Bob' }
    ];

    // Submit a plain value using a structured state envelope
    this.vault.mergeState({ value: employees });
  }
}`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
  }
);

employeeCell.initialize();

const employees = [
  { id: 1, name: 'Alice' },
  { id: 2, name: 'Bob' }
];

// Submit a plain value using a structured state envelope
employeeCell.mergeState({ value: employees });`}}
